content.thinking:
I'm planning out a wizard's bookshelf prop—about 2.2m tall, 1.2m wide, 0.4m deep—and thinking through whether I need a root joint for the builder API even without actual bone joints.

I'm settling on a high-fantasy anime aesthetic with cel-paint colors and gold trim, keeping flat colors under the 64 limit since paints don't count against it. Now I'm mapping out the actual dimensions: a frame roughly 1.4m wide, 0.42m deep, 2.3m tall, with side panels, a plinth base, and five shelf levels at specific heights, plus a back panel with a painted starry-sky texture using an SVG plane layered in front of the solid backing box.

Still working out the wood material -- leaning toward a rich indigo-blue grain paint with cel shading and gold accents for the trim, applied across the box geometries for the side panels and crown.

For the crown itself, I'm shaping a pointed gothic arch by extruding an outline traced in the XY plane -- defining points that curve up from the base through intermediate steps to a sharp peak, then extruding it as a slab to form the gable, finishing with gold trim details.

Now I'm planning a thin gold sweep along the arch's edge using offset polyline points, plus a star finial at the top and a glowing crescent moon on the crown's front, working out non-self-intersecting outlines for both shapes using arcs and offset circles.

I'm tracing the connection points between the outer and inner circle arcs, checking that the endpoints near 60° and 300° line up properly with the inner arc near 100° and 260°, keeping the inner shape nested correctly inside. This seems sufficient for the outline.

Now for the books, I'm designing a function that builds a standing book with spine facing forward: a cover box plus a slightly inset cream page block, with the pages peeking out at the back and top/bottom edges while the spine shows gold band details at the front.

With roughly 45 books at 5 parts each (gold bands, title plate, maybe a gem stud), that's around 225 parts plus shelf structure, keeping well under budget. I'm planning to reuse a shared palette of cel paints (around 10 colors) across books to limit texture atlas cost, using flat gold for bands and flat cream for pages to keep things simple.

For leaning books, I'm writing a helper function that places parts by rotating local coordinates around the base pivot using axis-angle rotation, so each book can tilt convincingly while keeping its base fixed.

For the spine detail, I'm positioning a thin decorative band box on the front face at the spine, roughly scaled to the book's thickness and depth, deciding to keep it flat rather than adding curvature for simplicity.

For embellishment, I'm adding a small dark title plate on the cover with a gold accent, plus planar rune-glyph decals (using transparent SVG textures with glyphs) placed just in front of the spine, making a few texture variants so books don't look identical, while noting rotation on leaning books won't affect the plane's facing direction.

Now I'm planning the overall frame structure: plinth, top moulding, side panels, shelves, back, crown, and fluted pilaster columns with gold capitals at the front corners, plus decorative gold filigree textures applied as planes on the outer side panels.

Writing SVG decoration patterns...

Now I'm working out the shelf geometry—board thickness and y-positions for each shelf level, plus the interior dimensions for the compartments where books will sit, including shelf depth and front edge trim.

Top compartment holds a crystal ball on a stand plus candles. Checking total height with crown and finial, I settle around 2.75-2.85m, which feels right for a tall wizard's bookshelf.

Now I'm planning shelf contents by tier: bottom compartment (0.16-0.60) gets large chained tomes in a leaning stack, and I'm working through what fills each level above that.

For floor props, I add a stack of books with a melted candle on top at one side and a tall pillar candle with wax drips on the other, widening the model's footprint slightly. Then I start laying out the first shelf's contents—thick tomes standing upright on the left and a row of flat books lying horizontally on the right, possibly topped with a scroll.

Continuing the shelf layout: S0 gets a lying stack of three books with a glowing blue orb on top plus leaning books at the right end, S1 has a scroll bundle in a basket, a row of books, and an orb on a brass stand with a candle, S2 features a crystal ball on a claw stand flanked by books with a candle on the side, and S3 starts with scrolls stacked pyramid-style alongside tall books.

I'm adding two glowing potion bottles to S3, then populating S4 with small books, candle holders, and tiny orbs. Now I'm writing a reusable candle-building function that assembles a cylinder body, drip details, a thin wick, and a glowing teardrop-shaped flame.

Adding candle holder dish...

I'm thinking the orb glow could use a small highlight sphere plus a swirling gradient texture mapped onto the sphere surface for that magical inner-swirl look, with distinct color variants for each orb (blue, violet, green/amber).

For the scrolls, I'm designing them as paper cylinders with darker spiral end-caps, wooden dowel rods extending past the ends with gold knob finials, and a thin ribbon band wrapped around the middle.

For potions, I'm designing a lathed bottle profile with a glowing liquid body, cork top, and gold neck band — keeping it simple with 3 bottles instead of adding labels. Thinking about skipping a hourglass but maybe adding a small telescope to round out the shelf decor.

Instead I'll add an armillary sphere: a small central orb with three intersecting gold torus rings at different radii and rotations, mounted on the base — a nice decorative touch. For the big tome on another shelf, I'm planning gold corner caps, a clasp lock plate, and a glowing gem to make it feel ornate and magical.

For books lying flat, I'm designing a reusable builder that stacks a bottom cover, pages block, and top cover with an embossed gold frame and glowing gem, including spine placement and rotation handling via a small helper function for positioning and orienting pieces in 3D space.

Still defining the Grp helper class...

Still working out typing...

I'm worried makeMesh might bake transforms directly into geometry data, so I should create fresh geometry per part rather than sharing references. Now I'm defining the wood and shelf materials with grain textures for the box palette, varying the axis and color tones for horizontal versus vertical surfaces.

I'm fleshing out the gold accent paint, book cover colors across ten hues, and spine plate treatment, deciding to reuse cover colors for spines with gold banding for variety.

Now I'm sketching the tome function itself, setting up its origin and parameters for lean, rotation, bands, runes, and gems, then working out how the cover shell and visible page edges should be constructed so the pages only peek out at the back face.

I'm trying slightly different page-box dimensions so the cream pages peek out from the covers at the top and sides without overlapping awkwardly at the back, adjusting the box depth and centering to avoid poking through where the spine should be solid cover.

Still working out the spine layout...

I'm estimating total part counts to stay under budget: with 40-45 books averaging around 6-7 parts each (bands, pages, cover, plate, rune), plus frame and other scene elements, I need to trim some optional details like plates to keep the overall count manageable around 850 parts.

I'm sketching rune texture SVGs with gold glyph strokes, then designing a helper function to place rows of standing books sequentially with gaps and occasional leaning variants.

For the leaning books, I need to figure out rotation pivots so the base stays grounded while the top tilts outward — adjusting the origin offset by half the thickness times the sine of the lean angle, and accounting for the extra x-shift at the top. Tall tomes in this compartment can reach up to 0.40 in height.

Working through the shelf clearances: compartment 0 spans 0.16 to 0.60 (0.44 clear), compartment 1 spans 0.64 to 1.06 (0.42), compartments 2 and 3 are similarly 0.42 each, and compartment 4 is tighter at only 0.25, so I'm capping book heights at 0.38 for those middle shelves. I'm working out the shelf tops at 0.16, 0.64, 1.10, 1.56, and 2.02, matching shelf centers of 0.14, 0.62, 1.08, 1.54, and 2.00 with 0.04 thickness, and confirming the plinth sits at 0.12 height to support the bottom shelf.

Now I'm laying out the plinth and crown structure: a front plinth box, side panels running from 0.12 up to 2.33, a top board slightly wider than the case for overhang, a cornice with a gold trim line, an arched crown piece, and a star finial capping the whole thing around y=2.78-2.85. I'm also placing decorative pilasters as cylinders at the front corners with gold capital rings top and bottom.

For added ornamentation I'm giving the pilasters thin gold bands at regular heights, bringing each pilaster to roughly 9 pieces including caps and bands. Then I'm turning to floor props on either side of the case: a stack of books topped with a candle and wax puddle on the right, and a tall candelabra with a central rod and pedestal base on the left.

For the candelabra I'm sweeping three curved arms off the central stem, each ending in a cup holding a candle. Then I'm shaping the flame itself as a lathe-generated teardrop profile, wrapped in a glow effect with an inner whiter core layered on top for brightness.

Writing candle geometry...

Still writing dish and wax geometry...

I'm now defining an orb-building function that places a glowing sphere with a highlight positioned for front-upper-left lighting, plus a lathe-based gold stand profile beneath it.

Still refining the stand's cup shape...

I'm checking shelf clearance with the orb radius and scaling factors to make sure the orb sits properly above the stand, then sketching a texture generator using a radial gradient SVG for the sphere's surface, working out how the UV coordinates map around the equator so the front-facing view shows the correct portion of the drawn pattern.

Writing SVG swirl pattern...

Writing scroll geometry code...

Skipping the ribbon tail, so total parts count to 7, with scroll count around 9 giving 63 total objects. For the parchment texture I'm sketching a spiral using concentric circles as a simpler approximation of a scroll pattern.

Now I'm designing the potion object: a lathe-generated glass bottle body with a glowing liquid, a cork cylinder at the neck, a small gold ring torus for decoration, and considering whether to add a label plane or skip it for simplicity.

Finishing the lathe outline closing back to the axis, then designing the crown decorations: a gold crescent on the arch front, a glowing star finial, two smaller flanking stars, and a blue glowing gem sphere nestled in the crescent's hollow.

Positioning the crown extrusion and its z-thickness to align with the cornice, keeping the gable recessed properly, then starting work on the gold arch trim tube.

Mapping out the polyline points for the gold trim following the top edge of the outline, offsetting them slightly outward so the sweep sits half-embedded; keeping segments straight rather than smoothed since the underlying outline uses sharp edges.

I'm also planning small gold cone spikes (crockets) positioned at the outline's peak points, pointing upward and outward, and working through how to convert those local outline coordinates into world-space positions.

For decoration, I'm thinking about adding a filigree texture to the crown face — maybe a transparent SVG with gold vine/star patterns sized to fit within the arch silhouette without spilling past its edges.

I'm reconsidering the arch crown height, settling on 0.42 instead of 0.34, and sketching a pointed ogee-style outline with coordinate points tapering from the base up to a sharp peak. Now I'm starting to lay out the SVG viewBox for this shape.

Working out the scaling from world units to a 1024px canvas, then placing the decorative elements: a central diamond/star, flanking spiral circles, a horizontal vine with leaves, and small stars — checking that each element sits low enough in the arch to stay clear of the curved boundary at its given x-position.

Now I'm positioning the plane texture for the crown relative to the cornice, confirming its base and center align with the top of the board, and noting the rectangle's transparent corners get cut by the arch alpha test. I'm also planning a gold trim for the plinth decoration and starting the side panel's filigree vine path for its texture.

Working out the vine curve coordinates and leaf placements for the side panel SVG, then sizing and orienting the texture plane on the side face so the drawing's orientation stays upright, considering a mirrored version for the opposite side.

I'm also planning the plinth gold inlay strip at the base, the side panels' plain wood interior faces, and deciding against extra embellishments like lanterns or sky-star glow for the shelf interiors.

For decoration I'm sketching hanging tassels off a couple shelf corners—a cord, a gold knot sphere, and a downward fringe cone tinted red—placed at the outer edges where they won't obscure the books, implemented as a small reusable tassel component.

Now I'm working out book placement with jittered depth and position so standing books sit near the shelf front with slight natural variation, using a seeded random generator and a row-building function that lays out book specs (thickness, height, depth, cover, extras) along a cursor and returns the resulting positions.

Still placing books and stacking a small orb on top, checking heights stay under the shelf limit, then laying out the standing row of books on the right side.

I'm also designing a flatBook helper that can render an ornate version with a gold frame, gem, and corner plates, planning to use it for the big decorative tome at the base of the stack.

Still building clasp and cover details...

Now I'm scaling the frame texture for a 512px canvas and planning the first shelf layout: a bronze vase holding tilted scrolls on the left side, working out the lathe-turned outline shape for the vase.

I settle on a scroll length of 0.28 so the top stays under the shelf clearance, with centers computed to keep the bottom resting at y=0.1. The tilt uses rz=90±8 degrees so the scrolls lean slightly off vertical while still rotating properly around their axis.

Now I'm placing three scrolls in the vase with small x/z offsets, then laying out a row of leaning books with varied widths and heights, followed by a candle on a holder and a second book cluster, finishing with a purple orb on a stand near x=0.5.

For the second shelf layer (yTop 1.10), I'm arranging a left-side row of five books with different sizes, then adding a leaning book at the end that tilts toward the row for support, working out the rotation direction so its top leans back against the stack.

Actually leaning that book risks clipping into the neighboring book's corner, so I'm reconsidering direction—maybe skip the lean entirely and just place a centered armillary sphere with flat book rows on either side instead.

For the right row I'm sizing six books to fill the span, then checking the leftover gap between the row and the armillary ring, filling it with a tall candle positioned to clear the ring's top.

Now moving to the next shelf section, planning a pile of horizontal scrolls stacked at the bottom left.

Positioning the scroll pile...

Still placing shelf objects...

Still building floor props...

Total height is landing around 2.85m, taller than a real bookshelf but fine as a stylized wizard's prop; I'll skip adding floor clutter like books or scrolls and keep it simple. I'm adding a wooden cornice box at the top with a gold trim strip and a row of small dentil blocks along the front edge.

I'm thinking about merging these repeated dentil boxes into a single geometry using mergeGeometries to cut down part count, and considering doing the same for the gold accent bands across all the books.

Extending this idea, I could collect every flat-gold-colored piece—bands, knobs, spheres, cylinders, torus, cone shapes—into one shared geometry collector, applying position and rotation transforms to each box before merging them all into a single gold part at the root joint, which would dramatically reduce the overall part count.

I'd generalize this with a color-keyed collector so cream or other-colored pieces merge the same way, flushing each color group into one merged part at the end; parts needing textures or glow stay separate, and even Paint-colored pieces can merge since their UV/position/normal data still works fine, using the Paint object itself as a map key.

Each geometry gets its transform baked in via a matrix before being pushed into the bin, and since all the primitive geometries share consistent position/normal/uv attributes, merging should work cleanly. I'm double-checking that merged geometries using paint colors still read correctly since the painted parts all share one material.

I'm now checking the bone/joint attachment logic — the root joint sits at the origin so that's fine — and verifying that applyMatrix4 correctly handles normal transformation when non-uniform scale is involved, which it does via the normal matrix. Next I'm sketching out a Grp class that builds a rotation quaternion from Euler angles, and I'm working through how three.js's 'YXZ' rotation order actually composes the axis rotations.

I'm designing helper methods for part construction — add, part, tex, and glo — to handle quaternion composition, texture mapping, and glow intensity for flat-colored materials, confirming that glow copies per strength work fine for solid colors. Now I'm also tallying up flat color usage across parts (gold, pages, dark plate, cork, wick) to stay under the material limit.

For textured rune planes on book spines, I'm setting up one plane part per book with shared materials keyed by texture and tint, then adding optional glow to specific books whose runes are marked to glow.

Now I'm defining the SVG rune textures, three variants with gold strokes sized for the texture resolution, laying out different glyph shapes per variant using lines, diamonds, and circles.

Still writing more textures for the cover frame, sides, crown, sky backdrop, spiral cap, and orb, plus considering extruding a star shape for the finial glow.

Drawing the crescent moon shape...

For the orb textures, I'm writing a helper that generates gradient-filled SVGs with swirl strokes and sparkle circles for each color variant, keeping white as the mesh highlight for the glow effect.

I'm now adding the small scene details: crystal cones on the shelf, gold armillary rings, candle flames with glow, and a few simple tassels, while skipping the chain and lock on the tome to keep things simple.

Actually the top of the cabinet works better — I'll place the candles on the cornice at either side, positioning them slightly forward so they clear the crown molding behind, and tuck the inkpot and quill off to one side at a similar depth so nothing overlaps the gold trim.

Now I'm defining the inkpot as a small lathe-turned shape with a narrow neck and flared lip, colored deep teal, and considering whether to add a faint glow for the ink and sketch out the quill next.

Working out the back panel dimensions and placement so it sits flush within the frame depth, then sizing the sky plane to roughly match its aspect ratio for the star field, accepting some stretch since it'll be partly obscured by shelves anyway.

I'm moving on to set up the imports and type definitions for the scene builder module, pulling in geometry merging utilities, path and paint helpers, and the toon/glow shading kits before defining the core types for colors and vectors.

Writing helper functions for geometry batching...

Writing the Grp helper class...

Still writing helper methods and checking type signatures for scale and transform options...

I'm working out how to type the lathe outline points for the arch shape, using tuples for coordinates and planning typed arrays for the outline literals.

Now I'm sketching a helper function for building a tome/book shape, with parameters for lean angle, rune glow, plates, and bands, computing the geometry based on position and dimensions.

I'm working out the page dimensions so they're properly inset from the cover on all sides, verifying that the page length, height, and center offset line up correctly given the cover thickness margins.

Now I'm adding gold spine bands near the top and bottom, and deciding on a simple rule to add extra thinner bands at the quarter positions when a flag is set, so some books get a fancier four-band look while others stay simple.

I'm also designing the decorative plate and rune symbol on the cover face: a dark plate centered on the spine, with a rune texture layered slightly in front of it, optionally glowing for certain books. Checking that the proportions still work for thinner book spines, then tallying up roughly how many geometry pieces each book will end up with.

Now I'm writing a helper function to lay out a row of books side-by-side, jittering their depth slightly for a natural lean, and cycling through cover colors, rune indices, glow flags, bands, and plates based on each book's index. I'm also defining the spec tuple type and making sure the cover and paint constants are set up as module-level resources so they don't need to be rebuilt per row.

I'm then building a flat book function: constructing top and bottom covers, a spine, and inset pages, carefully computing offsets so the pages sit recessed within the cover edges and fit between the top and bottom cover thickness.

I'm adding a textured page frame on top, a spine detail, and an optional glowing gem for ornate books.

Now I'm defining a candle function that returns the height and optionally builds a lathed gold holder dish beneath the wax, sized relative to the candle radius.

Adding handle, candle body with wax cylinder, randomized drip spheres along the rim, and a small wick cylinder on top.

Now I'm defining the flame shape with outer and inner glowing lathe outlines using a tapered point profile, scaled for a smaller inner core, then starting to sketch out a new orb-generating function.

I'm working out the geometry so the orb sits properly nested into the cup rim, solving for the sphere's center height so its radius matches the cup's rim circumference at the correct intersection point.

Now I'm placing the white sphere itself with a glow effect, then adding a smaller highlight ellipsoid offset toward the front-upper-right to simulate a specular shine, working out its position as a fraction of the radius along each axis.

I'm adding a second tiny highlight dot lower-left for added realism, then returning the cup's center height. I'm skipping decorative claws around the rim and considering just a simple detail ring, before starting to sketch the stand's outline profile as a series of coordinate points.

Checking those stand outline points for self-intersection... the segments near the top curve don't cross, so the shape holds up geometrically. Now I'm moving on to designing the armillary sphere's center orb.

The ring intersects the cup slightly but it's acceptable, so I'll keep only the horizontal and tilted rings and skip the small star beads. I'm now checking the armillary sphere's clearance, calculating the radius and center height so the top stays within bounds.

Now I'm writing the scroll function, which builds paper cylinders with spiral end caps, a central dowel, and gold sphere finials at each end.

Writing potion function code...

Writing crystal cone function...

I'll hang the tassels from the underside of shelf 2, placing them at x=±0.62-0.63 and z≈0.19 so they clear the vase and orb already on that shelf without overlapping nearby books.

Now I'm building a candelabra function: a lathed gold base, a tapered rod stem, beaded spheres along the stem at varying heights, and curved swept arms branching outward using catmull-rom paths.

Still placing book stacks and candle...

Thinking about whether to add leaning tomes near the shelf and an open spellbook, but deciding to skip those for budget reasons. I'm also considering small gold diamond studs along the plinth skirt for extra detail.

I lay out the rotated diamond studs across the plinth front and confirm the piece count works, then move to crown dentils beneath the top board, positioning them to protrude slightly as a valance over the compartment opening.

Now I'm placing cylindrical pilasters at the side edges, choosing darker wood with gold banding, checking they sit flush against the side panel front edge without protruding past the plinth, and adding capital caps where the pilaster meets the top board.

Writing SVG texture code...

Still writing side texture SVG...

Now I'm building the frame texture with a double-bordered rectangle, an eight-point star burst in the center, and small diamond accents at each corner, all colored in gold.

For the spiral orb texture, I'm layering concentric rings of varying radii over a base circle with a small dot at center, scaled so stroke widths render crisply at the final texture size. Then I'm starting the top-level build function, creating the builder and setting up the root joint for the bookshelf assembly.

Still writing structure helpers...

Now I'm setting up the paint palette, defining wood grain textures with different axes for sides versus shelves, and darker trim colors for plinth and cornice elements.

Rounding out the color palette for rocks, crystals, and flat elements like the plate, wick, and feather, plus orb texture gradients in blue, violet, green, and amber. Now I'm starting to place the frame geometry, beginning with the plinth box.

Adding shelf boxes...

Now I'm positioning the back panel with its dark color, checking that book pages sitting at depth don't clip through it, and setting up side planes. Then I'm extruding an arched crown shape at the top with beveled edges in the trim color.

Writing gold trim sweep...

Adding more finial details...

Checking the arch height at the crescent edges confirms it fits within the crown silhouette. I'm working out the crescent's rotation so its opening faces upward instead of sideways, adjusting the point angles by 90 degrees, and considering placing a glowing gem sphere in the hollow at the top center.

I'm positioning the crescent extrusion with its depth, offset, and gold paint color, then setting up a star finial shape with outer and inner radii above the crown, giving it a thin extrusion and a pale yellow glow color.

I'm placing a thin gold spire cylinder rising from the crown tip up to where the star finial sits, tweaking heights to keep the total structure near 2.9 meters, then adding two smaller glowing stars flanking the crescent at symmetric x positions along the arch.

I see the outer spiral overlaps the star region, so I'll remove the outer spirals and keep just the inner ones plus a horizontal vine with dots, confirming stars at ±0.4 work fine. Now I'm defining a helper to generate star point coordinates by alternating outer and inner radii at 36-degree steps, then adding a crown decal plane element.

Checking that the crescent and crown plane don't visually conflict since the plane has no art at its center, I now move to writing the full module: metadata export, texture type aliases, and a helper function for constructing point arrays.

Writing scaffold code...

Checking the overlap math for the leaning book against the last upright book, tracing where its tilted left edge lands relative to the book height.

Now stacking the flat books on top of each other with slight rotations and decreasing sizes, then adding a sphere on top, and checking the total height stays within the vertical bounds before it hits the ceiling limit.

For the right-side row, I'm computing cumulative widths of several books placed side by side to see if they overflow the boundary, adjusting the starting x-position and trimming the row to fit, then planning to add a candle after.

Now I'm shifting focus to a vase placement at the next shelf position, defining its lathe coordinates and color, then starting to add decorative paper scroll elements around it with their own positions, radii, segment counts, and colors.

Continuing to place the remaining books, candle, and orb while checking clearances against the vase and stand radii...

Adding the orb and right-side book row for shelf 2, then starting the scroll pile placement for shelf 3.

Still placing potions and verifying book row offsets, then starting the shelf 4 layout with another row of books computing cumulative widths.

Checking the orb and candle heights stay within the shelf ceiling, then positioning the crystal cluster with varying heights and colors on the small rock base.

I'm laying out the cornice decorations—candles, an inkpot with quill, and a blue orb—then noticing the candle's holder radius pushes its depth slightly past the front edge, so I'm adjusting the z-position inward to keep it within bounds.

Settling on the holder radius factor and z offset, then moving to the orb stand sizing and the inkpot setup with its quill shaft and feather vane geometry...

Still writing feather shape...

Now I'm planning the floor stack with candelabra and candle placement, and thinking about adding a round rug underneath for extra storytelling detail.

Adjusting rug sizing to roughly 2.3 by 0.6 units, positioned so the floor candelabra sits near but outside its edge, with a tiled texture built from a border frame plus a row of diamonds and stars in a wine-and-gold color scheme.

I'm checking the plane orientation and offsets to avoid z-fighting with the box top, verifying the rug sits flush with the floor and that objects placed on it remain correctly grounded. Now I'm preparing to write the final code carefully, watching for TypeScript strictness issues in the part definitions.

Building the crescent outline function...

I'm checking that the inner spiral points stay within the outer circle's radius so the shape doesn't self-intersect, verifying a few sample coordinates near the closing edge between inner point 100° and outer point 60°.

Now I'm writing a function to generate star outline points, alternating between outer radius R and inner radius r at each 36° step, marking outer points as sharp corners, and I need to make sure the tuple type for each point is explicitly typed to satisfy the OutlinePoint interface.

Outline orientation probably doesn't matter for extrusion. I'm now checking the z-depth math for the book/tome object -- making sure the front face position plus jitter minus the depth doesn't clip into the back panel, settling on a default front z of 0.15 with a small jitter range so the back face stays safely within bounds.

Now I'm generating the sky background with a seeded random generator, scattering around 110 small stars with varying radii and a mix of blue and warm-white colors, plus adding four-point sparkle shapes at some positions...

Still writing SVG code...

Still writing candle geometry...

Still writing object placements...

Now I'm tallying up the total part count across the scene to check it stays reasonable—books, scrolls, flats, and background elements all adding up.

Placing the hanging stars under the top board, checking their positions against the candles and crystals to avoid overlap, settling on x=-0.33 and x=0.27 as clear spots.
